newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on low liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on low liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended up 95 basis points on Friday at 18.25 percent on late speculation drived by month-end demand for liquidity, traders said.

"The market was under pressure today from month-end demand for liquidity, and some dealers took advantage to speculate by withholding cash until the last minute, which is why rates increased," a dealer said.
A fixed-income analyst said recent Banco de Mexico intervention had also led to liquidity shortages in the market.
"Banco de Mexico has pumped a lot of paper into the market and drained a lot of liquidity this month, which has squeezed the market," one analyst said.
The central bank has since April drained surplus liquidity through direct Cetes sales combined with repos. Previously, the bank's preferred method was to auction cash deposits at shorter maturities.
On Friday, Banco de Mexico drained a total of 1.816 billion pesos through three direct Cetes sales and three repos.
Traders added that late speculation and liquidity shortages stopped secondary rates from following the downward trend in U.S. long bond yields.
U.S. Treasury bond yields had gained 26/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed 15 basis points higher on the day at 19.00 percent.
Liquidity of 1.249 billion pesos was due to flow back into the system on Monday from prior central bank participation.
